uslaw-usc-t2-s132a2:
Section 132a–2 of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with funds for the goods of the Library of Congress. It sits in Chapter 5, on the Library of Congress. The goods in view are chairs and tables, and gear for the office and for the library. In the year of funds 2001, and in each year from then on, the Librarian may move funds. That power is in aid of any like power given by a second law.

The funds that may be moved are those granted to the Librarian for a set end. That end is the buy, the set-up, the keep, and the repair of the goods named. The funds may be moved to and among the accounts of the Library that are free for use. Sums so moved are to be joined with the account they go to.
uslaw-usc-t2-s136a2:
Section 136a-2 of Title 2 of the United States Code fixes the pay of the Librarian of Congress and the Deputy Librarian of Congress. It sits in Chapter 5 of Title 2, on the Library of Congress, in the text current through Public Law 119-134. The section opens with a broad override: it applies notwithstanding any other provision of law.

Under it, the Librarian of Congress is paid at a yearly rate equal to the rate of basic pay for positions at level II of the Executive Schedule. That schedule is set under section 5313 of Title 5. The Deputy Librarian is paid at the greater of two rates. One is the rate in effect for level III of the Executive Schedule, and the text goes on to name the other measure of comparison.
